body:
Advisor disposition on the independent Codex review of #2248/#2249. Both PRs remain UNMERGED per
your instruction.

AC4 — NOT SUSTAINED. The finding was "help text still doesn't disclose blocking TUI behavior". It
does, verbatim, at the top of `aida agent new --help` on the PR head:

  "This lane spawns an INTERACTIVE agent in the foreground and BLOCKS until that agent's session
   exits. A vendor TUI does not exit when its turn ends — it returns to its prompt — so a seat that
   has finished its work still holds this command."

AC4 asks: "If the interactive lane keeps blocking, its help says so." That is met. It landed in
bcd7822d28 via #2247, which is already merged, and #2249 was rebased onto that, so it is present at
abc02552. I suspect the reviewer read a released binary rather than a branch build.

BUT checking the claim properly surfaced a REAL defect the review missed, in the very next sentence:

  "`aida agent status` shows `idle` for a seat that is waiting at a prompt rather than working."

That is FALSE, and BUG-1704 is the proof — `classify_status` returns Busy whenever any live lease
covers the worktree, which for the main checkout is effectively always. The help text sent the
operator to the one column that cannot answer the question. Fixed in 304ca777b1: it now points at
the CPU column and says explicitly not to trust `status` for this, with the reason. So the finding
was wrong and the inspection was still worth doing.

AC5 — the literal text was about REPORTING ("the signal should be something the substrate reports"),
and the CPU column reports it. But the reviewer's underlying objection is fair: the headline `status`
still says busy, and leaving AC5 text on BUG-1701 while BUG-1704 owns the work is exactly the trap
where a spec keeps gating on text that has already moved. So rather than argue it, I made it
structural: `aida edit BUG-1701 --carve-out <AC5> --carve-into BUG-1704`. AC5 is now OUT of
BUG-1701's description with a typed carved-out-to edge, so the obligation has one owner and the
disposition is not buried in a comment.

SCOPE NOTE for the next review pass: #2249 is the ROUTING fix ("nothing steered the orchestrator to
the one-shot lane"). AC1–AC3 were already satisfied by shipped machinery before this session —
`aida do` routes by groomed mode, and drain runs `spawn_claude_headless`, which returns an
ExitStatus. Reviewing #2249 against all of BUG-1701's ACs conflates it with #2247's already-merged
content.

#2248 — the review found no code issue at b9b13fed, and Build has since PASSED. #2249's Build passed
at abc02552; 304ca777b1 is now re-running.

NON-AUTHOR REVIEWER: understood that the GitHub review could not post because the CLI authenticates
as you, the PR author. I have not merged either PR and will not. Both need a non-author GitHub
reviewer. Worth noting the same constraint will recur for every PR an agent opens under your
credentials — that is a fleet-wide gap, not a property of these two.
